brief: A single hex base, nothing else added beside or on top of it, with five drawers in it.

requirements.requirement: A single hex base, with nothing else added beside or on top of it
requirements.evidence: One Hex base half (half-n, north half) at cell 0,0. No covers, caps, bins, or other parts were added beside or on top of it. The check reports meshClash clear with only an info note that three faces could take caps, which I left open as asked.

The configurator offers only one drawer site per half base (on its cut face). A full base has no cut face, so it takes none. I placed one drawer (drawer:0#0,0#cut) on the half base. No further drawer site appeared after that, so five drawers cannot be placed on a single base.

finish.summary: I built a single hex base as a north half-base with one drawer on its cut face. Nothing else was added. The configurator allows only one drawer per half base, so the five-drawer requirement is not met. Five drawers would need five separate half bases, which conflicts with the single-base brief. The build is clear of mesh collisions.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
